html:
Lin Zexu was the commissioner the Qing emperor sent to Guangzhou in 1839 to end the opium trade. Foreign trade was confined to that one port under the Canton system. That year he made foreign merchants hand over more than 20,000 chests of opium and destroyed them. With two colleagues he then wrote to Queen Victoria, asking her to stop the trade at its source. Within a year the two countries were fighting the First Opium War.

We have heard that in your own country opium is prohibited with the utmost strictness and severity … Since then you do not permit it to injure your own country, you ought not to have the injurious drug transferred to another country, and above all others, how much less to the Inner Land! Of the products which China exports to your foreign countries, there is not one which is not beneficial to mankind in some shape or other.
Let us suppose that foreigners came from another country, and brought opium into England, and seduced the people of your country to smoke it, would not you, the sovereign of the said country, look upon such a procedure with anger, and in your just indignation endeavor to get rid of it? Now we have always heard that your highness possesses a most kind and benevolent heart, surely then you are incapable of doing or causing to be done unto another, that which you should not wish another to do unto you!

The letter is not known to have reached the queen.
